newsitem.title: USA: Florida judge limits punitive claims on tobacco companies.
newsitem.headline: Florida judge limits punitive claims on tobacco companies.

text.p: The judge in Florida's Medicaid lawsuit against the tobacco industry Tuesday sharply limited the amount of punitive damages that may be sought in the case.

Palm Beach County Circuit Judge Harold Cohen restricted punitive damages, but let stand claims for triple damages on alleged racketeering by the tobacco companies being sued by Florida for taxpayer money spent on treating sick smokers.
In addition, Cohen said Florida could pursue limited additional damages if it can prove fraud by tobacco companies through advertising or false claims made after 1982.
The trial is scheduled to begin Aug. 4.
Florida had argued it was entitled to punitive damages as well as compensation for money spent treating smokers through the Medicaid health insurance programme for the poor.

But Cohen said a Florida law passed in 1994 that is the main vehicle for the state's lawsuit did not allow for punitive damages, only actual damages. The fraud claims are being brought under a separate law, the judge said.

The judge ruled that Florida can pursue triple damages if it wins its case under another Florida law. The state claims the tobacco companies conspired to hide the dangers of smokeing from Americans and sold them dangerous products.

A landmark $368.5 billion settlement between state attorneys general and cigarette makers reached Friday prompted speculation that Florida's case might not come to trial, but attorneys representing the state and Florida officials have said they plan to go ahead with their case.
